defaults.validation_not_required_because: A tokenizer is a model artifact, not a corpus. There are no rows to split.

notes: Published tokenizers, as first-class owned artifacts. A tokenizer is the single most essential dependency of a token corpus - the shards are meaningless integers without it - so it is published INTO the airlock and pretrain/curriculum datasets depends_on it, rather than pinned by reference to a HuggingFace repo that can be force-pushed, gated, or deleted out from under every dataset that relied on it. That reference-pin was the exact dangling-dependency failure the standard exists to kill (DATASET-STANDARD.md sections 0 and 7), just pointed at HF instead of /scratch. THE PAYOFF: vocab_size and eos_token_id stop being hand-typed guesses. The validator loads the published tokenizer.json (a few MB, published once, referenced by everything) and COMPUTES them via tokenizer_v1.derive_vocab - rule 0.4, recompute-never-trust - and the pretrain-tokens decode smoke test asserts every sampled token id against that DERIVED bound, so a wrong-dtype or corrupted shard is caught against the real vocabulary rather than a placeholder. A tokenizer group must contain tokenizer.json; other HF tokenizer files (merges.txt, special_tokens_map.json, tokenizer_config.json) may ride along. Name it corpus/method plus the axis that distinguishes it (tokenizer/dolma2-bpe, tokenizer/cosmo2-tokenizer) - never a bare word. license.basis is an honest 'unknown' because tokenizer terms vary upstream; override per tokenizer with the actual, checked license. No token format defaults here on purpose: a tokenizer is not token data, it is the key that makes token data legible.
